title: Psychoanalytic Theory (Freud)
summary: Freud's psychoanalytic theory: the topographical model (conscious/preconscious/unconscious), the structural model (id/ego/superego), psychosexual stages of development, defence mechanisms, and the role of unconscious conflict.
objectives: Describe Freud's topographical and structural models.
Explain id, ego and superego functions.
List the five psychosexual stages and fixation effects.
revision: Freud's psychoanalytic theory: topographical model (conscious/preconscious/unconscious), structural model (id/ego/superego), psychosexual stages, defence mechanisms.
traps: id = pleasure principle; ego = reality principle; superego = moral principle.
Five psychosexual stages: oral, anal, phallic, latency, genital.
Fixation at any stage shapes adult personality.

notes.t: The mind is divided into conscious, preconscious and unconscious levels. The unconscious holds repressed memories, desires and conflicts that influence behaviour outside awareness.
The Structural Model: id, Ego, Superego
The primitive, instinctive component operating on the pleasure principle, seeking immediate gratification.
The rational component operating on the reality principle, mediating between id demands and external reality.
The moral component internalising parental and societal standards, striving for perfection.
The ego balances the id's impulses, the superego's moral demands and reality. Failure produces anxiety and defence mechanisms.

i: Latency (6–puberty): dormant sexual feelings, social skills

r: Redirecting emotions to a safer target
Shouting at family after a bad day at work
Attributing one's own unacceptable feelings to others
Accusing others of being hostile when one is hostile
Reverting to an earlier developmental stage

notes.t: UGC NET frequently tests id/ego/superego functions, psychosexual stages and fixation, and defence mechanisms.

mnemonics.title: IEC-PLG
mnemonics.text: I — id (pleasure), E — ego (reality), C — conscious/preconscious/unconscious, P — psychosexual stages, L — libido, G — defence mechanisms
